question: Does the OdontoForge exact-search architecture reduce explored state growth on preregistered hard SAT families, and how does transient-state lifetime behave as n grows?

anatomy.enamel: independently verified SAT certificate or exact terminal closure
anatomy.regeneration: replacement of dead/conflicting branch from still-live frontier without dropping exact branches

controls: held-out instances not used to tune search ordering

hard_families.parameters: clause/variable ratio centered near the hard region; freeze seeds before run

hard_families.role: proof/search stress control when generator is frozen and independently checked

stages.pass: Odonto status matches independent exact baseline on all feasible small instances and every SAT certificate verifies independently.
No branch required for exactness is pruned by score, entropy, CRYSTALLIZE, INJECT_CHAOS, or regeneration policy.
Any claimed search reduction survives frozen held-out instances and is reported with full failures/variance.
Report empirical slope of log2(nodes+1) versus n with confidence/dispersion; never label sub-1 finite slope as polynomial proof.
Actively search for families where Odonto loses its apparent advantage or returns toward exponential growth.

transient_state_exit_clock.entry: branch creation after a decision or propagation event
transient_state_exit_clock.lifetime_measure: number of branch-growth/propagation steps from entry to terminal exit
transient_state_exit_clock.purpose: Test whether branch lifetime contains reusable predictive structure about search difficulty; this is an algorithmic observable only.

cross_domain_reference.allowed_use: shared abstract bookkeeping and hypothesis generation only
cross_domain_reference.forbidden_use: biological evidence as support for a complexity claim

promotion_rules: performance claim requires preregistered metric plus holdout replication
complexity-class claim requires a formal general proof
P_VS_NP remains OPEN until such proof exists
next_action: Run G0 on small frozen instances, then freeze the first hard-family seed manifest before inspecting G2/G3 performance.
